landmarks.name: Dubrovnik Old Town
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its well-preserved medieval walls and historic architecture.

landmarks.name: Plitvice Lakes National Park
landmarks.writeup: Famous for its cascading lakes and waterfalls, this park is a natural wonder and a UNESCO World Heritage site.

landmarks.name: Diocletian's Palace
landmarks.writeup: An ancient Roman palace in Split, serving as a historical and architectural landmark.

landmarks.name: Pula Arena
landmarks.writeup: One of the best-preserved Roman amphitheaters, still used for events and concerts.

landmarks.name: Zagreb Cathedral
landmarks.writeup: The tallest building in Croatia, known for its Gothic architecture and historical significance.

cultural_events.name: Dubrovnik Summer Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event featuring theater, music, and dance performances in historic settings.

cultural_events.name: Ultra Europe Music Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A major electronic music festival held in Split attracting international artists and visitors.

cultural_events.name: Sinjska Alka
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional knights' tournament held annually in Sinj, celebrating Croatian heritage.

cultural_events.name: Zagreb Film Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An important cultural event showcasing regional and international films.

cultural_events.name: Motovun Film Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An independent film festival held in the hilltop town of Motovun, focusing on auteur cinema.

food_writeup: Croatian cuisine varies by region, featuring Mediterranean influences along the coast with seafood, olive oil, and fresh vegetables, while inland areas emphasize meats, stews, and hearty dishes. Popular foods include nevapi, peka, and fresh Adriatic fish.
brief_history: Croatia has a rich history influenced by Roman, Byzantine, Venetian, and Austro-Hungarian empires. It became part of Yugoslavia in the 20th century and declared independence in 1991, leading to the Croatian War of Independence. It joined the European Union in 2013.
current_conflicts: Croatia is currently stable with no active internal or external conflicts.
